Issues.Title: Add ListBox BeginUpdate/EndUpdate batching tests and fix SetItemsCore leak
Issues.Body:
This PR fixes a ListBox redraw suspension leak during failed data-binding refreshes and expands regression coverage for update batching.

## Changes

Ensures SetItemsCore calls EndUpdate in a finally block, restoring redraw even when item population throws.
Adds tests for nested batches, handle creation and recreation, disposal, exception recovery, and native selection consistency.

## Customer Impact

- A data-binding refresh that throws while populating the list no longer leaves the ListBox permanently unpainted.

## Regression?

- No

## Risk

- Low. Only the `EndUpdate` call moves into a `finally`; the normal path is unchanged.

Issues.Title: Fix issue 15419:DomainUpDown/NumericUpDown renders incorrectly in WinForms Designer with Padding set in VisualStylesMode: Classic
Issues.Body: Fixes #15419 ## Root cause UpDownBase uses the Opaque control style, which suppresses normal background painting. In classic button-layout mode, non-empty Padding leaves areas around the child edit and button controls that may not be painted, causing them to display an incorrect or stale background. ## Proposed changes Paint the clipped client area with the appropriate background color in OnPaint when classic button layout is active and Padding is non-empty. For disabled controls without a custom background color, use SystemColors.Control. Add bitmap tests covering visual styles, border styles, enabled state, custom background colors, clipping, and the Paint event. ## Customer Impact Controls with non-empty Padding in classic button-layout mode will render their exposed padding areas with the expected background color, avoiding unpainted or stale-looking regions. Controls with zero padding or modern side-by-side buttons are unaffected. ## Regression? - No ## Risk - Mini ## Screenshots ### Before ### After https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6577d422-c21a-4885-99a6-ea482828a885 ## Test methodology - Manual - Automation test cases - ## Test environment(s) - 12.0.0-alpha.1.26555.106 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/15420)

Issues.Body: ### .NET version 11.0 ### Did it work in .NET Framework? Not tested/verified ### Did it work in any of the earlier releases of .NET Core or .NET 5+? No ### Issue description The DomainUpDown control renders incorrectly in Designer when Padding is applied. Unexpected background areas and visual artifacts appear around the control. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a .NET 11 WinForms project. 2. Set VisualStylesMode = Classic. 3. Add a DomainUpDown control to the form. 4. Set AutoSize = true. 5. Set Padding = 15 (or another non-zero value). 6. Observe the control in Designer. 7. Run the application and compare the appearance.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0] Add opt-in native clipboard text fallback for WPF
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes dotnet/wpf#11968 in conjunction with the corresponding WPF changes in dotnet/wpf#12125.

## Proposed changes

- Add an internal, default-disabled policy allowing WPF to opt into native clipboard text fallback. WinForms explicitly remains opted out.
- Support the opt-in fallback in the .NET Framework shared-core target as well. 
- Combine the original managed source with a captured native OLE reader. Read from the managed source first, then use the native reader if needed for `Text`, `UnicodeText`, and `OEMText`. For sources that don't support typed reads, typed text reads go straight to the native reader.
- For composed clipboard wrappers, forward single-argument `GetData` and `GetDataPresent` calls to the overloads with `autoConvert: true`, matching .NET 9. This also applies to non-text formats, but native fallback is still limited to plain text.
- Preserve custom-payload identity, managed format enumeration, and writes. Add six regression cases covering WinForms clipboard behavior before and after flushing.

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- Enables WPF to restore Windows text synthesis when managed clipboard sources disable automatic conversion, addressing missing text availability and retrieval reported in dotnet/wpf#11968.
- Preserves existing WinForms behavior: unflushed clipboard data retains managed conversion semantics, while flushed data exposes Windows-synthesized formats.

## Regression?

- Yes - supports fixing a .NET 10 WPF regression. No intentional WinForms behavior change.

## Risk

- Low for WinForms because the fallback policy remains disabled. Moderate for opted-in consumers because shared clipboard composition and retrieval paths change. Native fallback is limited to plain-text formats and keeps the captured proxy's owning adapters alive.

<!-- end TELL-MODE -->

- Automated test execution and CTI manual validation.

Issues.Title: Fix MonthCalendar test failures across midnight
Issues.Body:
Fixes test failures in build: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1671901&view=ms.vss-test-web.build-test-results-tab

Prevents flaky date assertions by deriving test dates from each calendar’s initial selection. Adds coverage for selection behavior with and without a native handle.

**Fix:** Derive relative dates from each calendar’s initial  SelectionStart  inside the test. This covers min/max date and selection tests, with and without a native handle.

Issues.Title: WFO3011/WFO3012: Suggested VB fixes can introduce build errors and change runtime behavior
Issues.Body:
Helllo,

At DevExpress, we maintain a significant amount of Visual Basic code across our products and published materials. We've noticed that the newly introduced VB diagnostics affect a substantial portion of this code, including code in demos, project templates, and product documentation.

While testing .NET 11 RC2, we encountered several issues with the new WinForms Designer analyzers, particularly **WFO3011** and **WFO3012** (as well as WFO3001).

Given the number of affected places, reviewing and fixing everything within a reasonable timeframe would be challenging. More importantly, some of the suggested fixes are not safe to apply mechanically.

We have prepared four minimal repro projects demonstrating the issues: [WinForms-VB-Analyzer-Sample-Issues.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34684359/WinForms-VB-Analyzer-Sample-Issues.zip)

## Problems identified

### 1. Backing field collision (WFO3011 → BC31060)

WFO3011 suggests changing a regular component field to `WithEvents`:

```vb
Private button1 As System.Windows.Forms.Button
```

However, `WithEvents` makes the VB compiler generate a hidden `_button1` backing field. If the user partial class already contains a member with that name, the build fails with **BC31060**.

### 2. Setter collision (WFO3011 → BC31060)

A similar issue occurs if the class already contains a method named `set_button1`. The compiler-generated setter accessor conflicts with the existing method, resulting in **BC31060**.

### 3. Generic event handler (WFO3012 → BC32080)

Consider this valid VB event subscription:

```vb
AddHandler button1.Click, AddressOf HandleButtonClick(Of Integer)
```

WFO3012 suggests replacing `AddHandler` with a `Handles` clause. However, VB does not allow generic methods to be used as `Handles` event handlers, resulting in **BC32080**.

The workaround is to introduce a non-generic forwarding handler manually.

### 4. Event subscription timing changes (WFO3012 → silent behavior change)

This is the most concerning issue because the suggested fix builds successfully but changes runtime behavior.

With `AddHandler` at the end of `InitializeComponent`, the event subscription happens after component properties have been initialized.

With `Handles`, the handler is subscribed as soon as the field is assigned. Consequently, property setters executed later in `InitializeComponent` can trigger the handler during initialization.

In our repro, the handler is invoked once after applying the suggested fix, whereas it is never invoked with the original code.

We encountered this in one of our project templates: after the mechanical fix, a navigation panel becomes hidden when it should be visible.

## Why this matters

Both `AddHandler` inside `InitializeComponent` and private component fields without `WithEvents` are legitimate, long-standing VB patterns. They are used by code generators, third-party designers, serializers, and existing applications.

Many VB WinForms applications have 15+ years of accumulated code. For their developers, upgrading to .NET 11 could mean fixing hundreds of build errors, manually reviewing affected forms, and re-testing initialization behavior.

The four cases above demonstrate why this migration cannot be handled safely through a bulk replacement or an automatic code fix.

## Suggested changes

We would appreciate reconsideration of the default severity and applicability of these diagnostics:

1. **Make WFO3011 and WFO3012 warnings or suggestions by default** for existing projects, rather than errors that break the build after a simple TFM change. Alternatively, consider enabling them as errors only for new projects.
2. **Account for cases where the suggested fixes are unsafe**, including generated member name collisions, generic event handlers, and changes to event subscription timing.
3. **Document the migration implications**, including behavioral differences and how developers can opt out of these diagnostics, in the .NET 11 breaking changes documentation.

We understand the goals behind the new Designer analyzers and want to support more predictable Designer serialization. However, we believe this should not come at the cost of breaking otherwise valid existing VB applications or silently changing their behavior.



We previously had a [similar discussion regarding WFO1000](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/issues/12476) and appreciated the team's willingness to revisit its scope. We hope we can find a similarly practical solution here.

Issues.Title: [WinForms .NET 11] Button initial render displays square/rectangular artifact corners before mouse hover under VisualStylesMode.Net11
Issues.Body: ### Environment Visual Studio 2026 Release: Novemer 2026 Feature Update Channel: Stable Version: 18.12.0 Instance: 7e99fbcb ### .NET version 11.0 (GA Release) ### Did this work in a previous version of Visual Studio and/or previous .NET release? This is not regression but first time implemention in .net 11 ### Issue description When opting into the new .NET 11 modern renderer using Application.SetDefaultVisualStylesMode(VisualStylesMode.Net11);, standard Button controls exhibit unstyled, legacy rectangular/square corner artifacts on initial form launch. Once the user hovers over the button (triggering a MouseEnter / MouseLeave event or manual invalidation), the control correctly repaints and displays the expected modern Windows 11 rounded corner geometry. ### Steps to reproduce Initialize a .NET 11 Windows Forms application in Program.cs: C# ApplicationConfiguration.Initialize(); Application.SetHighDpiMode(HighDpiMode.PerMonitorV2); Application.SetDefaultVisualStylesMode(VisualStylesMode.Net11); Application.SetDefaultFormRevealMode(FormRevealMode.Deferred); Place a standard Button on a form (FlatStyle = Standard, UseVisualStyleBackColor = true). Launch the application. Observe the sharp rectangular/square corner outlines visible around the button upon initial render. Move the mouse cursor over the button and away—the button instantly snaps to correct rounded corners. Expected Behavior: Standard buttons should render with the modern .NET 11 rounded corner geometry immediately upon initial form creation and display, without requiring a mouse hover event to force a repaint. Actual Behavior: Buttons render with cached legacy square/rectangular border artifacts on initial launch until an interactive mouse event forces a redraw. ### Diagnostics ```text N/A - Visual rendering artifact only. No exceptions, warnings, or trace output are generated in the Output window during initial handle creation. Environment details: - .NET Version: .NET 11 - Visual Studio Version: Visual Studio 2026 Enterprise - OS: Windows 11 - Renderer Mode: VisualStylesMode.Net11 ```

Issues.Title: [release/10.0] Fix issue 15213: Bitmap finalized during Image.Save(Stream, ImageFormat) leaks native GDI+ memory
Issues.Body:
Backport of #15254 to release/10.0

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/issues/15213

## Proposed changes

Within `CoreImageExtensions.Save(this IImage image, Stream stream, ...)` of `System.Private.Windows.GdiPlus`, wrap `GdipSaveImageToStream` in a try/finally block and call `GC.KeepAlive(image)` in the finally block.

## Customer Impact

The correction avoids abnormal native memory growth in `Save(Stream, ImageFormat)` under high-pressure/specific GC timings, reducing memory risks and potential stability issues in long-duration or batch image processing scenarios.

The impact on existing behavioral compatibility is minimal (only extending object survival to the end of the method), and should not change functional results or introduce visible behavioral differences.

- Yes - regression PR: #10783 or #10784
